skill.name: alchemist
skill.description: Build, test, and publish Olbrain chat agents, automated jobs, agent teams, and research agents. Check existing builds and connect live agents to websites or applications.
skill.summary: Manage Olbrain agent builds, review tests and approvals, and connect live agents.
skill.author: olbrain

security_audit.summary: Most static matches are Markdown notation, documented service links, or secret storage guidance; the server integration does use an organization-wide credential. The review found risks in approval defaults, support disclosures, browser-facing routes, and staff uploads. No evidence of an attempt to manipulate this audit was found.

remediation.issue: Host execution mode is treated as approval for cards.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit confirmation for publishing, paid runs, and consequential changes. Enforce this in the service even when host approvals are disabled.

remediation.issue: Platform gap reports send requirements without review.
remediation.suggestion: Preview a minimal, redacted support report. Name the recipient and obtain explicit approval before sending it.

remediation.issue: App routes use a broadly scoped credential and omit caller controls.
remediation.suggestion: Use a key scoped to the intended agent. Enforce request authentication, session ownership, input limits, and usage quotas before making upstream calls.

remediation.issue: The staff upload command interpolates service response data.
remediation.suggestion: Upload through a structured HTTP client without invoking a shell. Validate the destination against approved HTTPS hosts and keep the write link out of logs.

semantic_findings.title: Host auto mode substitutes for deployment consent
semantic_findings.description: The skill says to "answer every card yourself in auto mode" by default. This can approve ordinary publish or make-live actions without separate user consent.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The default and the publish path are explicit. Browser and client confirmations protect some actions but do not cover every card.

semantic_findings.title: Platform gap reports share requirements without review
semantic_findings.description: The skill tells the assistant to send the user's exact requirement to Olbrain support without asking first. Requirements may contain confidential business or customer information.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The text explicitly requires reporting before notifying the user and exempts these reports from the normal support ticket workflow.

semantic_findings.title: Browser integration omits caller and session controls
semantic_findings.description: The proposed server route accepts browser input and a session ID without specifying caller authentication, session ownership checks, or usage limits. A deployment without those controls could allow unauthorized runs, charges, or access to another conversation.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The integration shows what the route accepts but does not specify those safeguards. Actual exposure depends on the generated code and where it is deployed.

semantic_findings.title: Staff upload trusts tool data in a shell command
semantic_findings.description: The staff workflow inserts upload response values into a shell command without specifying input validation or safe argument passing. Unsafe substitution could execute unintended commands or send the archive to a wrong destination.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The command uses response fields directly and documents no validation. The issue is limited to the staff workflow and depends on how the command is constructed.

content.value_statement: Building an agent requires tracking its requirements, tests, and approvals. Alchemist guides those steps and helps teams connect an approved agent to a website or application.
actual_capabilities: Start or resume builds for chat agents, automated jobs, agent teams, and research agents.
Check build progress, review test results, and surface pending approval cards.
Publish agents through the Alchemist build workflow.
Show a read-only diagram of a draft or published agent version.
Retrieve connection steps for a live agent, including website chat or a server integration.
Open or follow up on Olbrain support tickets when the user asks.
limitations: Requires signed-in access to the Olbrain tools and permission in the active organization.
Available connectors and actions depend on the organization, build state, and client tools.
Test commands and live runs can use credits. Some confirmations and sign-ins must happen in the browser or a client dialog.
Screen tools are limited to verified Olbrain staff accounts.

best_practices: Confirm the active Olbrain organization and agent before making changes.
Use approved test data and require explicit consent before paid runs, support reports, or publishing.
Use browser sign-in for connectors and keep application credentials on the server.
anti_patterns: Pasting API keys, passwords, or signing secrets into the chat.
Treating host auto mode as permission to publish or make a billed run.
Assuming that a draft or successful test means the agent is live.

faq.question: What can I build?
faq.answer: Alchemist supports chat agents, automated jobs, agent teams, and research agents. Check its capabilities for the channels and connectors you need.

faq.question: Do I need an Olbrain account?
faq.answer: Yes. You need signed-in Olbrain tools and access to the organization where you want to work.

faq.question: Can I resume an earlier build?
faq.answer: Yes. Give the build label so the skill can find it. If several builds match, the skill asks you to choose.

faq.question: Can tests cost credits?
faq.answer: Yes. Test commands and live runs can be billed. Ask to review the expected effects before approving a run.

faq.question: How should I provide a connector secret?
faq.answer: Use the browser approval flow for connector secrets. Keep application keys in server settings and never paste them into chat.

faq.question: Can anyone build an Olbrain screen?
faq.answer: No. Screen tools are limited to verified Olbrain staff accounts. Connecting screen roles also requires an eligible organization role.
